title: Axis Bank Revises NRI Fixed Deposit Rates: How FD Plus Compares to Standard FDs
excerpt: The bank non-withdrawable FD Plus product offers up to 7.10% for NRE deposits, but the liquidity trade-off matters for diaspora investors weighing their options.
body:
• Axis Bank's latest NRI FD rate revisions offer up to 6.25% on standard NRE fixed deposits and up to 7.10% on its FD Plus product for larger deposits
  • NRI FD Plus offers higher returns but does not permit premature withdrawal, making it unsuitable for depositors who may need emergency access to funds
  • NRO deposits offer rates up to 6.85% for the 1-year sweet spot tenure, but unlike NRE deposits, interest earned on NRO accounts is taxable in India
  • FCNR(B) deposits in US dollars offer 4.00% for 1-2 year tenures and up to 6.00% for 3-5 years, providing a hedge against rupee depreciation

What Changed in the Latest Revision

Axis Bank has updated its fixed deposit interest rates for Non-Resident Indians across multiple product categories through a series of revisions in 2026, with the most recent NRE rate card effective July 24, according to the bank's published rate schedules.

The revisions span three NRI deposit products: standard NRE and NRO fixed deposits, the higher-yielding NRI FD Plus, and FCNR(B) deposits in foreign currencies. For NRIs evaluating where to park rupee savings or hedge dollar earnings, the differences between these products are material.

Standard NRE and NRO Deposits

For standard NRE fixed deposits under 3 crore rupees, Axis Bank offers 6.25% per annum for the popular 1-year to 1-year-10-day tenure. Rates climb to 6.50% for 15-18 months and top out at 6.60% for tenures of 18 months and above. For deposits of 3 crore rupees and above, the 1-year rate rises to 6.85%.

NRO deposit rates follow a similar structure. Shorter tenures carry lower rates, rising from 3.00% for 7-14 days through 5.75% for 9 months to 1 year. The 1-year NRO rate for deposits under 3 crore rupees is 6.25%, identical to NRE. For deposits in the 25-50 crore rupee range, the 1-year rate reaches 6.85%.

The critical distinction: NRE deposit interest is fully tax-exempt in India and freely repatriable, while NRO interest is taxable at 30% (plus cess) under the Income Tax Act, with repatriation limits of up to $1 million per financial year.

FD Plus: Higher Returns, Zero Flexibility

Axis Bank's NRI FD Plus product targets depositors willing to lock in funds without the option of premature withdrawal. In exchange, rates run 25 to 50 basis points higher than standard FDs across most tenures and deposit sizes.

For NRE FD Plus deposits, the 1-year rate starts at 6.60% for the 3-5 crore rupee slab and reaches 7.10% for deposits of 25 crore rupees and above, based on the rate card effective July 31. The standard NRE FD offers 6.85% at the same tenor and deposit size, a 25 basis point gap that widens at shorter tenures.

The no-withdrawal condition is the deal-breaker for many NRI depositors. Those parking education funds, emergency reserves, or money earmarked for a near-term property purchase in India may find the liquidity restriction too steep for an extra quarter-point of yield.

FCNR(B): The Dollar Hedge Option

For NRIs earning in foreign currencies and wary of rupee depreciation eroding their returns, Axis Bank's Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits offer a third path. USD-denominated FCNR(B) deposits earn 4.00% for 1-2 year tenures and up to 6.00% for 3-5 years. GBP deposits fetch 4.10-5.90%, while Canadian dollar deposits offer 2.30-4.50% depending on tenure.

FCNR(B) deposits are denominated and repaid in the original foreign currency, eliminating exchange rate risk. Like NRE deposits, interest is tax-free in India, making them attractive for NRIs in higher US tax brackets who can also claim foreign tax credits.

How to Choose

The decision between standard NRI FDs, FD Plus, and FCNR(B) comes down to three variables: liquidity needs, tax efficiency, and currency view. Standard NRE FDs offer the best balance of decent returns and flexibility. FD Plus makes sense for large deposits that can be locked away for the full tenure. FCNR(B) works best for those who expect the rupee to weaken against their earning currency or who want to avoid conversion risk entirely.

All rates remain subject to change without notice, and NRIs should compare current offerings across major banks before committing. SBI, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank have all revised their NRI deposit rates in recent months.
